verdicts.explanation: Without retries a single 429 from the supplier fails the whole nightly sync.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Retry with exponential backoff honouring Retry-After (e.g. urllib3 Retry on a requests Session).

verdicts.explanation: fetch_inventory is declared to return list[Item] but returns None, so sync() never has real data and len(None) raises TypeError.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Implement the supplier call (requests.get(SUPPLIER_URL, params={'since': since}) and map rows to Item), or raise NotImplementedError until it exists.

verdicts.explanation: A failed fetch is swallowed, so the job continues with no data and fails later with a misleading error instead of the real cause.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Catch requests.RequestException, log it with context and re-raise (or return 0 explicitly) instead of pass.

verdicts.explanation: breakpoint() in a scheduled job blocks waiting for a debugger; under cron or a worker pool the sync hangs forever.

new_issues.title: `items` is unbound when the fetch fails
new_issues.explanation: If fetch_inventory raises, the except branch swallows it and items is never assigned, so this line raises NameError and hides the original error.
new_issues.suggested_fix: Assign items inside a branch that always runs (e.g. items = [] before the try) or re-raise in the except block.
